full_judgment: 8. Further reference may be made to the case of Sanmukh Singh and Others-Vs. King, reported in AIR 1950 (PC) 31-wherein it has been held that "Criminal P.C. (1898), S. 195(1)(C)- Section refers to production of document itself and not its copy -Copy of forged document given in evidence -absence of complaint under this section is no bar to trial. Section 195(1)(C) only refers to a document alleged to be forged and not to a copy of it. The reason is that the Court before which a copy of a document is produced is not really in a position to express any opinion upon the genuineness of the original. Though by production of a copy secondary evidence of the contents of a document might be said to he given, the forged document itself cannot be said to be given in evidence. A.I.R. (12) 1925 Oudh 413, Approved.
